Tokyo Shinjuku-Shibuya 5-Day Itinerary Overview
This 5-day plan (May 15-19, 2025) centers on Shinjuku and Shibuya districts, blending iconic sights, parks, shopping, and nightlife with daily meals under $50/person. Travel via efficient Tokyo Metro (get a Pasmo/Suica card); expect mild spring weather around 20C/68F with possible light rain.

Trip Planning Context
Dates align with mid-May cherry blossom tail-end and moderate crowds pre-summer peak. Assumes central Shinjuku/Shibuya base for 10-20 min walks/trains between sites; budget excludes transport (~$10/day) and entry fees (~$5-15/site). Restaurant picks verified for ~$30-45/person including tax/service via current reviews.

Daily Itinerary Breakdown

| Day | Date | Morning (9am-12pm) | Lunch (~$40/person) | Afternoon (1-5pm) | Dinner (~$45/person) | Evening (6pm+) |
|-----|------|--------------------|---------------------|-------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| 1 | May 15 | Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (cherry blossoms, ponds) | Omoide Yokocho yakitori stalls (grilled skewers, beer) | Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free panoramic views) | Robot Restaurant alternative: Ichiran Ramen Shinjuku (tonkotsu ramen set) | Golden Gai alley bars (tiny pubs, casual drinks) [1][3][5] |
| 2 | May 16 | Yoyogi Park & Meiji Jingu Shrine (serene walks, people-watching) | Harajuku crepes at Marion Crepes (sweet/savory, ~$15) then explore | Takeshita Street (quirky shops, street fashion) | Gyukatsu Motomura Shibuya (breaded beef cutlet DIY, reserve) | Shibuya Scramble Crossing & Hachiko statue at sunset [1][3][6] |
| 3 | May 17 | Kabukicho exploration (neon signs, arcades) | Shinjuku izakaya at Torikizoku (all-you-can-eat skewers ~$25) | Shibuya Sky observatory (360 views, book ahead) | Soba at Sagatani Shibuya (handmade noodles, seasonal veggies) | Shibuya Parco shopping & Pokemon Center [3][6] |
| 4 | May 18 | Harajuku Omotesando (designer architecture, cafes) | Okonomiyaki at Sakura-tei (cook-your-own savory pancake) | Cat Street to Shibuya (boutique shops, street art) | Tonkatsu at Butagimi (premium pork cutlet, book ahead) | Nonbei Yokocho (hidden bar alley near Shibuya) [3][5] |
| 5 | May 19 | Shinjuku shopping (department stores, electronics) | Tsukemen at Fuunji (dipping noodles, quick line) | Free time: Shibuya Loft or Loftwork for souvenirs | Yakitori at FUKU (grilled chicken skewers, intimate) | Depart or night views from Shibuya Scramble Square [1][3] |

Dining Spotlight
Three standout recommendations (all under $50/person, cash/card, English menus available):
1. Gyukatsu Motomura (Shibuya): Crispy beef cutlet you grill tableside with rice/veggies (~$35). Reserve via Tabelog.
2. Ichiran Ramen (Shinjuku): Customizable spicy tonkotsu in private booths (~$20). 24/7, iconic.
3. Butagimi (near Harajuku): Juicy tonkatsu with cabbage slaw (~$45). Michelin-mentioned, advance booking essential [3].
